metadata.title: Data Density Pass 10 -- Day 3 Final Positions and Aftermath (Ticks 601-675)
metadata.description: Individual regiment records for the final positions after Pickett's Charge repulse through the end of the battle. Survivors on Seminary Ridge. Union regiments holding Cemetery Ridge. Both armies in their last positions. East Cavalry Field units. The 38 survivors of the 1st Minnesota. The 26th NC survivors. End of battle at tick 675.

placements.notes: 19th Massachusetts -- helped seal The Angle breach. Devereux led them in without orders.
38 survivors of 1st Minnesota. Held the line all three days.
16th VT made two bearing changes today. First against Pickett's right. Then against Wilcox.
12th NJ -- fired buck-and-ball into Pettigrew's men at close range
Garnett's 8th VA -- about 80 survivors. Garnett dead. Body never identified.
Armistead's 9th VA -- Armistead died July 5. His hat still on his sword.
26th NC -- started July 1 with 843 men. Now 140. Still in line.
52nd NC -- Marshall killed in the charge. These are the survivors.
Kemper's 1st VA -- some of the last men Stannard's Vermonters hit from the flank
Brockenbrough's survivors -- broke while others advanced. A shame that follows them.
Greene's 137th NY on Culp's Hill -- held two days and nights
Stonewall Brigade -- 12 assaults on Culp's Hill. Jackson's old regiments.
Steuart's 3rd NC -- 42.5% casualties across three days
END OF BATTLE. 20th Maine on Little Round Top. 130 casualties. The left of the Union line held.
END OF BATTLE. 38 survivors of the 1st Minnesota. All three days in line.
END OF BATTLE. Webb's brigade at The Angle. The wall held.
END OF BATTLE. Stannard's Vermont Brigade. Two wheels. The charge broken.
END OF BATTLE. 26th North Carolina. 843 to 140 across July 1 and 3.
END OF BATTLE. Armistead's 9th VA. Their general died beyond the wall on July 5.
END OF BATTLE. Armistead's 14th VA. The regiment closest to Cushing's guns.
END OF BATTLE. Greene's 137th NY. Culp's Hill never fell.
END OF BATTLE. Stonewall Brigade. 12 assaults. Jackson's men.
